sentences.text: He filed this Crl.M.C under Section 528 BNSS praying for quashing all further proceedings against him.
The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Sections 376 and 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 119(b) of the Kerala Police Act.

2. The prosecution case is that the accused, with an intention to satisfy his sexual lust, after promising to marry the de facto complainant, repeatedly committed rape upon her and took her nude photographs in his mobile phone and thereafter failed to marry her.

3. According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, even if the entire allegations levelled against the petitioner as such is believed, the same will not amount to the offence punishable under Section 376 IPC.
Therefore, he prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioner.
4. The petition was strongly opposed by the learned 2026:KER:20257 Public Prosecutor.
5. Though notice was served on the 2 nd respondent/de facto complainant, she did not turn up.
6. On a perusal of the FI statement, it appears that the petitioner and the de facto complainant become friends while they were working in a hotel.
Thereafter as requested by the petitioner, she stayed along with him in a hotel room.
It was in the said room, the petitioner allegedly committed rape upon her.
7. From the FI statement, it is revealed that, she accompanied him to different hotels on different dates even after the 1st incident.
It prima facie shows that the relationship between them was a consensual one.
From the 164 Cr.PC statement given by the de facto complainant also, it is revealed that the relationship between them was a consensual one.

Therefore, as argued by the learned counsel for the petitioner, the allegations levelled against the petitioner does not make out the offence punishable under Section 376 IPC.
8.

Though the offence under Section 119(b) of Kerala Police Act is also alleged, there is no evidence to show that the mobile phone of the petitioner was examined with the help of an expert to ascertain Jerin vs State Of Kerala on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129687396/
2 whether it contained any nude photographs of 2026:KER:20257 the de facto complainant.
9. In the above circumstance, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings against the petitioner, as the same will only be an abuse of the process of the Court.
Therefore, this Crl. M.C is allowed.

All further proceedings against the petitioner in S.C No.1793 of 2024 of Additional District and Sessions Court (Violence against Women and Children), Ernakulam,
arising out of Crime No.289 of 2024 of Nedumbassery Police Station, is quashed under Section 528 BNSS.
